results.meaning: Rate across a gut-cell monolayer: a proxy for oral absorption.
Whether an oral dose reaches the bloodstream intact.
Octanol/water partition: drives membrane crossing and off-target stickiness.
Aqueous solubility; an insoluble compound cannot be dosed.
Human intestinal absorption.
P-glycoprotein inhibition; affects absorption and drug-drug interactions.
Blood-brain barrier penetration — wanted for CNS targets, unwanted otherwise.
Plasma protein binding; only the unbound fraction acts.
Volume of distribution: how far the compound spreads beyond blood.
CYP2C9 inhibition — a drug-drug interaction risk.
CYP2D6 inhibition — a drug-drug interaction risk.
CYP3A4 inhibition — the most common interaction liability.
Whether CYP2C9 metabolises it.
Whether CYP2D6 metabolises it.
Whether CYP3A4 metabolises it.
How long it survives in the body; sets the dosing interval.
Microsomal clearance — how fast the liver removes it.
Acute toxicity in rodents.
hERG channel blockade — the cardiac-arrhythmia liability that kills programmes.
Mutagenicity in the Ames test.
Drug-induced liver injury.
